newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt officials on EU tour before trade deal.
newsitem.headline: Egypt officials on EU tour before trade deal.

text.p: Egypt and the European Union resumed talks on an association agreement on Wednesday with their sights on a meeting of European and Mediterranean foreign ministers in Malta next month.

The head of the Egyptian delegation, Gamal Bayyoumi, told reporters Egypt would like to tell the Malta meeting they had laid the groundwork for the agreement, which would lead in the end to free trade in manufactured goods and services.
"Both sides have the political will to reach agreement before the Malta conference... It would be hard to go to Malta without agreeing on the basic principles," he said.
The agreement, similar to those the EU has signed with Morocco and Tunisia, would not liberalise agricultural trade because of European protectionism in this sector.
Egypt has been holding out for larger quotas for its agricultural exports to Europe, arguing that the balance even of agricultural trade is heavily in Europe's favour.
The Europeans have gradually raised the quotas on offer for rice, potatoes, citrus fruit and cut flowers but not yet enough to satisfy the Egyptian side.

"An agreement must meet the balanced interests of both sides, especially as the Europeans account for 46 percent of Egypt's foreign trade," added Bayyoumi, who toured Europe with Supply and Trade Minister Ahmed Gueily earlier this month to argue Egypt's case at ministerial level.
